title: Google Antigravity SDK Adds Local Model Support for Greater Token Efficiency and Code Privacy
key_facts: Google added support for local models in the Antigravity SDK, so developers can run agent workflows on their own machines and mix in cloud models for high-level tasks.
It uses an Architect-Builder pattern: a cloud model plans and splits the task using filenames and descriptions without seeing source code; local builder agents do the code work.
In a demo patching three vulnerable Python modules, Google reports only 95 of about 3,400 tokens were used in the cloud and 97.2% locally, with no source code uploaded.
The first implementation runs Gemma 4 26B A4B through Google's LiteRT; it also supports OpenAI-compatible local servers such as Ollama, LM Studio and vLLM.
A Reddit commenter noted the recommended 24GB+ of VRAM or unified memory is a real gate and that speed and cost were not benchmarked.
The SDK is distinct from the Antigravity IDE, which is built on it.
quote_evidence: Google has introduced support for local models in the Antigravity SDK, enabling developers to build and execute agentic workflows directly on their own machines
only 95 out of approximately 3400 tokens were used on the cloud for planning, while the remaining 97.2% were spent locally.
Google also states that no source code was uploaded to the cloud.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers can keep source code on their own computers while a cloud model only does the planning.
notes: InfoQ reports Google's claims; figures come from a single Google demo. Announcement date not stated in the article.
